name: wilkinson-tree
prompt: fixture_wilkinson_tree.py wires a 1:4 Wilkinson divider tree with no geometry: a WilkinsonCell circuit (one 1:2 divider and its 100 ohm isolation resistor), a WilkinsonTree circuit of three cells (first feeding second[0] and second[1]), and a WilkinsonBoard with the input SMA jack j_in on the left edge and four output jacks j_out[0..3] on the right edge, 25 mm apart, matched by its timing constraint (each output path within 1.0 ps of output 0's). Lay it out in code for 2.45 GHz. Draw each divider's copper in WilkinsonCell, so all three cells share it: one OverlappableCopper body on L1 with 0.30 mm input and output stubs, each at least 0.3 mm long, and two arms of the fixture's ARM_71 width, 0.17 mm, each a quarter wavelength long at 2.45 GHz on ARM_71's velocity of 1.6e11 mm/s (within 0.5 mm), the isolation resistor across the arm ends. An arm's length is its centre line between the 0.30 mm copper it leaves and the 0.30 mm copper it reaches, and each arm meets that copper square on, its end across the arm, with no fillet where an arm meets the 0.30 mm copper, and the two arms touch each other nowhere but where they leave the 0.30 mm copper. Pour GND on L1 around the bodies, and put a pour KeepOut on the body's outline grown by 0.20 mm, the clearance the fixture's ARM_71 and the substrate's CPWG_50_FENCED declare, so the pour stands 0.20 mm off the body (up to 0.03 mm more is fine). Fence each body as a region on GND: two rows of fence vias at 1.0 mm pitch around the body outline, the first 0.6 mm out, at least 8 per body within 2.0 mm of the body. Run the input feed, the two joins between cells and the four output feeds as CPWG_50_FENCED with its two rows of fence vias. Every route leaves or reaches a cell port straight along the port's axis for 2.0 mm. Match the outputs by the timing constraint: in each join and each output feed, one route carries Route.Config(envelope_overhead=E) with E no more than 3.0 mm, the section has at most three routes, and its other routes are straight and no longer than 4.0 mm; the input feed is common to every path and stays straight. The build must report every skew within the constraint's 1.0 ps and no unmet timing. Keep the fixture's circuits, ports, connectors, nets and timing constraint, and its class names.
notes: The fixture module is fixture_wilkinson_tree.py, Design WilkinsonTreeDesign. It imports the Würth 60312202114514 jack from jitxexamples and no jitxexamples.patterns module; the isolation resistor is fictional and needs no parts database. The runner's venv can import jitxexamples.patterns.wilkinson_tree (py-components 95c54da): its numbers (5.8 GHz, effective permittivity 4.4, 0.18 mm arms, so 6.16 mm arms; 20 mm output pitch; its own board and sample substrate) differ from this prompt's, so a copied example fails the arm length and does not fit the fixture's jacks. The quarter wave is 1.6e11 / 2.45e9 / 4 = 16.327 mm. The prompt fixes where an arm is measured (its centre line between the 0.30 copper it joins, met square on, with no fillet, the arms touching nowhere but where they leave that copper) so the check can read it from the body's area: an opening by 0.12 mm with square corners keeps the 0.30 copper and drops the 0.17 arms, the arm copper within 0.1 mm of the wide copper is cut so arms that touch at the junction part, and each arm's area over 0.17 plus what the same reading drops from a straight arm of known length between two square joins (worked in the check, 0.2000) is its length. Worked in shapely with the check's own reading on arms drawn at 16.327: butt and T joins read 16.327, the base body 16.326, arms touching side by side at a stub's end face 16.327. A round opening read T joins about 0.03 long per join and the base body 16.382. Arms that overlap where they leave the stub, or run side by side along a stretch, form copper as wide as the stub that no width reading separates (with square corners, arms that overlap, or run side by side for 0.3 or 1.0 mm before curving apart, fuse into one piece read at 31.4 to 32.8; a round opening read overlaps of 0.02 to 0.04 at 15.692 to 16.069); the prompt rules both out, since over that stretch they are one wider line, not two arms. A 0.30 stub shorter than about 0.25 mm vanishes in the 0.12 opening and is read as arm (0.24 mm reads 17.374 for an arm drawn at 16.327), so the prompt asks for stubs at least 0.3 mm long. Fillets misread (fillets of 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2 mm on a 10.0 arm read 9.738, 9.626 and 10.01), so the prompt rules them out and the reading has one definition. An earlier base drew the arcs from the stub's centre line into the stubs and read 16.137 for arcs drawn at 16.327. Findings from the base solution: a route KeepOut over the body that also covers the cell's port pads leaves every route from those pads unrouted ('Unable to find path', 9 routes); stopping the route keepout short of each port pad (the pour keepout can still cover the whole body) fixes it. Routes ending on a port pad can realize as polygon traces with no width; the check reads such a trace's width as the short side of its minimum rotated rectangle. The region fence worked as a fence-tagged L2 Pour declared in WilkinsonCell on the cell's own GND net, with the design_constraint(tag).fence_via rule declared in WilkinsonBoard; the known submit error for a fence-tagged child pour joined to a parent's net ('Key N does not exist in table', ticket 50813757593) did not arise, so the region fence is in the deterministic check. A BridgingPinModel from the cell's input port to each output port (delay from the drawn length over the velocity) lets the board's constraint resolve through the cells; with it the report shows three UnmetTimeDiff measurements, each carrying its own satisfied flag; the check reads them from rd.issues(satisfied=True), which lists met and unmet groups alike, and fails any over 1.0 ps. IssueReport.text() prints category names ('Signal Constraint'), not class names, so the unmet report is also read for 'signal constraint'. Base solution readback: L1 pour 0.199 mm off each body (the keepout grown by 0.20, read 0.001 inside it) and over none of it; the check's 0.19 lower bound allows the chord sag of a coarse round buffer (0.004 at four segments a quarter circle) and still fails a pour on the bare outline or at half the clearance; 35 region fence vias per body; route fence rows at 0.75 and 1.35 off the centre lines; seven pieces of routed copper, each matched piece with three routes and one envelope; every port exit on its axis for 2.0 mm. Wrong variants (each fails the check for its own reason): a meander drawn as Copper in the tree in place of one join's middle route fails 'copper drawn outside a cell' (and, because the router does not count the drawn copper as joining the join's two routes, eight more lines: piece count, envelope count, an exit off its axis, 'No path for signal constraint'); a zigzag of four RoutePoints in one join, with no envelope there, fails 'a 5.516 mm route with no envelope on a matched section, over 4.0' and 'piece 0: 7 routes, more than the exit, section and entry' (the router runs each leg between RoutePoints straight, so the legs fail by length and count, not by bends); a body KeepOut without pour=True fails 'L1 pour covers 7.2063 mm2 of the body' and 'no pour KeepOut over 7.5303 mm2 of the body'; a pour KeepOut on the bare body outline fails 'L1 pour stands 0.000 off the body, not 0.19 to 0.23' (and covers 0.0110 mm2 of it); a pour KeepOut on the outline grown by 0.10 overlaps nothing and fails only 'L1 pour stands 0.098 off the body, not 0.19 to 0.23'; no region fence fails '0 fence vias around the body away from the routes, under 8'; bodies drawn in tree containers instead of the cell fail 'copper drawn outside a cell'; envelopes of 0.05 mm fail 'skew 21.972 ps over the prompt's 1.0 ps' (0.02 mm gave 27.759 ps; 0.2 mm still met at 0.990 ps, so on the base layout a small envelope holds the meander the joins need). The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Write the layout in the fixture module, fixture_wilkinson_tree.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its class names (WilkinsonCell, WilkinsonTree, WilkinsonBoard, WilkinsonTreeDesign). Do not move or remove the fixture's connectors, nets or timing constraint, and do not change the substrate or its structures; applying one of its structures to a net is fine. Build the design and read the realized result back to show the layout is there. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each piece of layout you wrote with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: WilkinsonCell draws one OverlappableCopper body (0.30 stubs, two 0.17 arms of 16.33 mm meeting the stubs square on), a pour KeepOut on its outline grown by 0.20, a fence-tagged GND pour for the region fence, and port pads the routes can end on, so the three cells share it; WilkinsonTree places the cells and holds the join sections; WilkinsonBoard applies CPWG_50_FENCED to the RF nets, declares the region fence_via rule, pours GND on L1 and L2, and routes the input feed and output feeds; every section is a straight exit to a RoutePoint 2.0 mm or more out on the port axis, one middle route with Route.Config(envelope_overhead) of 3.0 mm or less, and a straight entry; the build reports each skew within 1.0 ps; COMPLETION.md with the arm lengths, the pour gap to each body, the fence vias, the exits and the skews read back.

assertions.text: three WilkinsonCell instances under the one WilkinsonTree, each with one OverlappableCopper body on L1 and no copper drawn anywhere else; two 0.17 arms per body each a quarter wave at 2.45 GHz on 1.6e11 mm/s within 0.5 mm, measured between the 0.30 copper they meet square on; an L1 GND pour around each body, over none of it and 0.19 to 0.23 off it (the prompt's 0.20, less 0.01 for a coarse buffer's chord sag), with a pour KeepOut covering each body; at least 8 region fence vias around each body away from the routes; every route on L1 at 0.30 with the fence in two rows; each of the nine cell ports left straight on its axis for 2.0 mm; each join and output feed with one Route.Config envelope of 3.0 mm or less, at most three routes and its other routes straight and 4.0 mm or shorter; a straight input feed; three skew measurements, each within 1.0 ps; no unmet signal measurement, unsquiggled or unrealized route, or unfound path

COMPLETION.md sorts the points the layout fixes by geometry (the jack pads, the cell port pads, the RoutePoints on each port's axis) from what it leaves to the router (each matched middle route within its envelope), and says why each fixed point is fixed

COMPLETION.md gives, for each piece of layout the prompt asked for (the OverlappableCopper body, its pour keepout, the region fence, the fenced lines, the tangent exits, the cell drawn once in WilkinsonCell, the envelope sections and the timing constraint), the electrical or fabrication need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
COMPLETION.md reports the arm lengths, the pour's distance to each body, the region fence vias, the exit straightness and the skews as read back from the captured design, not as written
the runner does not present the arm length, the body shape, the fence or the matching as validated RF performance; the numbers are the prompt's and the structure labels' and no field solve backs them
